'''BNS ''Bangabandhu''''' ({{lang-bn|বানৌজা বঙ্গবন্ধু}}) is a [[Frigate|guided-missile frigate]] of the [[Bangladesh Navy]]. She is currently based at [[Chattogram]], serving with the Commodore Commanding BN Flotilla (COMBAN). She is currently the only frigate of the Bangladesh Navy armed with [[Anti-submarine warfare|ASW]] [[torpedo]] and gun based [[CIWS]].

==Armament==
This vessel has the [[Otomat]] Mk 2 Block IV [[anti-ship missile]]s on board the vessel which has a range of {{convert|180|km|mi}}.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.mbda-systems.com/product/otomat-mk2/ |title=OTOMAT MK2 BLOCK IV - MBDA |work=MBDA |access-date=2021-03-02 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In April 2018, Bangladesh Navy issued a tender for replacing two 40 mm [[DARDO|Fast Forty]] guns on board the ship with new 40 mm twin-barrel  gun system.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dgdp.gov.bd/dgdp/AP_TEN/s_doc/2241.pdf |title=Tender Specification Replacement of 2 X 40 L 70 Naval Gun - BNS Bangabandhu |publisher=DGDP |access-date=2 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403112442/http://dgdp.gov.bd/dgdp/AP_TEN/s_doc/2241.pdf |archive-date=3 April 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
''Bangabandhu'' was named after Bangladesh's founding father, [[Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]], who is popularly called ''Bangabandhu'' (Friend of Bengal).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rozario |first=Rock Ronald |date=18 March 2021 |title=Bangladesh still far from achieving founding father's dreams |url=https://www.ucanews.com/news/bangladesh-still-far-from-achieving-founding-fathers-dreams/91801 |access-date=2021-03-19 |work=Union of Catholic Asian News |type=Opinion |language=en}}</ref> The ship was ordered in March 1998. She was [[Keel laying|laid down]] on 12 May 1999 at [[Daewoo|Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering]], [[Republic of Korea]]. She was launched on 29 August 2000, and [[Ship commissioning|commissioned]] on 20 June 2001.<ref>{{cite book |editor-last=Saunders |editor-first=Stephen |year=2014 |title=Jane's Fighting Ships 2014-2015 |publisher=IHS Jane's |location=Coulsdon, UK |page=52 |isbn=978-0-7106-3101-5}}</ref>

In 2007 she was recommissioned again under a new name, as BNS ''Khalid Bin Walid''. Later on in 2009 she was renamed BNS ''Bangabandhu''.

The ship participated in Exercise Ferocious Falcon, a [[Military exercise|multinational crisis management exercise]], held at [[Doha]], [[Qatar]] in November 2012. While transiting to the exercise, the frigate visited the port of [[Kochi]], [[India]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Kochi/bns-bangabandhu-berths-at-kochi/article4066686.ece |title=BNS Bangabandhu berths at Kochi |work=The Hindu |date=5 November 2012 |access-date=24 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140518224831/http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Kochi/bns-bangabandhu-berths-at-kochi/article4066686.ece |archive-date=18 May 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref> The ship took part in [[Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training#CARAT Bangladesh|Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training(CARAT)]], an annual bilateral exercise with [[United States Navy]], from 2011 to 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.theindependentbd.com/printversion/details/17385 |title=US-Bangla jt exercise begins today |work=The Independent |location=Dhaka |date=30 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001075733/http://www.theindependentbd.com/printversion/details/17385 |archive-date=1 October 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 August 2013, the ship received the ''National Standard''.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://newsworld365.com/2013/08/29/pm-confers-national-standard-to-bns-bangabandhu/ |title=PM confers National Standard to BNS Bangabandhu |work=NewsWorld365.com |date=29 August 2013 |access-date=25 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001183849/http://newsworld365.com/2013/08/29/pm-confers-national-standard-to-bns-bangabandhu/ |archive-date=1 October 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2014, [[Malaysia Airlines Flight 370]], a [[Boeing 777#777-200ER|777-200ER]], went missing while in flight. Due to the possibility of finding the wreckage in the [[Bay of Bengal]], ''Bangabandhu'', along with the frigate {{BNS|Umar Farooq|1976|2}}, joined the search operation in the region.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/bangladesh-sends-2-navy-ships-to-verify-mh370-wreckage-claim-22435 |title=Bangladesh sends 2 navy ships to verify MH370 wreckage claim |work=The Daily Star |date=2 May 2014 |access-date=24 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150504155928/http://www.thedailystar.net/bangladesh-sends-2-navy-ships-to-verify-mh370-wreckage-claim-22435 |archive-date=4 May 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 31 May 2016, she started for [[Colombo]], [[Sri Lanka]] with 150 tonnes of relief for the victims of the floods and landslides caused by [[Cyclone Roanu]]. The relief included drugs, water purifying machines, pure drinking water, tents, food items and generators. She also joined the rescue efforts there.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://m.bdnews24.com/en/detail/bangladesh/1160532 |title=Bangladesh Navy's ship starts for Sri Lanka with more aid for flood victims |work=bdnews24.com |date=31 May 2016 |access-date=1 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701003459/http://m.bdnews24.com/en/detail/bangladesh/1160532 |archive-date=1 July 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The ship left for [[Qatar]] on 22 February 2018 to take part in 6th ''Doha International Maritime Exhibition and Conference (DIMDEX-2018)'' to be held from 12  to 14 March 2018. She paid goodwill visits to [[Mumbai Port Trust|Mumbai port]], in India, from 2 to 5 March 2018 and to [[Colombo Harbour|Colombo port]] in Sri Lanka from 22 to 25 March 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thebangladeshpost.com/national/22031/pdf |title=BNS Bangabandhu sails for Doha |publisher=The Bangladesh Post |date=22 February 2018 |access-date=22 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180223051257/http://www.thebangladeshpost.com/national/22031/pdf |archive-date=23 February 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 29 March 2018, she returned to her homeport, Chattogram.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ispr.gov.bd/কাতারে-অনুষ্ঠিত-আন্তর্জা/ |script-title=bn:কাতারে অনুষ্ঠিত আন্তর্জাতিক সমুদ্র মহড়া ও প্রদর্শনীতে অংশগ্রহণ শেষে দেশে ফিরেছে নৌবাহিনী যুদ্ধজাহাজ ‘বঙ্গবন্ধু’ |publisher=ISPR |date=29 March 2018 |access-date=21 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808091652/http://www.ispr.gov.bd/%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%85%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B7%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BE/ |archive-date=8 August 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>
